Candidate active/passive landbase-status source layers

Source: R/reportingPolygons.R
landbaseLayers.Rd

The per-FMA landbase-status ("active/passive", a.k.a. "contributing/non-contributing") coverages, each fetched, dissolved by status, and clipped to the study area by buildLandbasePolygons(). This generalises the per-study-area landbase processing formerly hard-coded across the LandWeb_preamble study-area helpers (SprayLake.R, WestFraser.R, Tolko.R, SundreFP.R, Manning.R).

landbaseLayers()

Value

A tibble with columns key, NAME_SHORT, tenure, source, id, layer, and status_col.

Details

A landbase coverage belongs to one tenure (not every tenure has one), so tenure holds that tenure's curated short name (tenureShortNames()): buildLandbasePolygons() fetches a source only when its tenure is present in the study area, avoiding the download of large (multi-GB) coverages that could not intersect it anyway. status_col is the source attribute holding the landbase status; layer names the layer for multi-layer File Geodatabases (NA = the source's only/first layer). NAME_SHORT discriminates a tenure's several coverages (West Fraser's three CLS supply blocks); it need only be unique within a tenure, since the reporting-unit name is "<tenure> <NAME_SHORT>".

Note

Gating was formerly a regex (applies_to) matched against the study-area name, which silently stopped matching anything once study areas became ecoregion groups ("WesternAlbertaUpland" matches no company name), so no landbase was ever fetched. Gating on the tenures actually present restores it.
